standard_prerequisites.name: The mapping cone of a function between sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: For f : A -> B the mapping cone C_f is the pushout of f : A -> B along A -> 1, with constructors t : C_f, iota : B -> C_f and alpha_1 : prd{a:A} iota(f(a)) = t, presented in the statement by its pushout diagram.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted equivalence is stated between f being an epimorphism, C_f being contractible, and f being surjective; the proof runs induction on C_f (source lines 198-211).

standard_prerequisites.name: Categorical monomorphisms and their equivalent formulations
standard_prerequisites.statement: For f : hom_A(a,b) in a category A, being a monomorphism is equivalent to the contractibility of sm{h:hom_A(x,a)} (f o g = f o h) for all x and g (clause (iii) of book Lemma 10.1.1).
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof applies the dual of that clause at source line 217 to obtain a path between the two pairs (iota, refl) and (const_t, alpha_1); the lemma and its proof are retained as context, so the reference resolves inside the package.

standard_prerequisites.name: Set-coequalizers and the universal property of the 0-truncated coequalizer
standard_prerequisites.statement: The coequalizer of f, g : A -> B in the category of sets is the 0-truncation of the homotopy coequalizer, and its universal property is the contractibility of sm{k:Q->C} (k o c = h).
standard_prerequisites.use: Retained as part of the context because it fixes the categorical language in which the epimorphism side of the equivalence is read.

core_obligations: From epimorphism to contractible cone: show prd{x:C_f} x = t by induction on C_f, which reduces to the two clauses I_0 : prd{b:B} iota(b) = t and I_1 : prd{a:A} opp(alpha_1(a)) . I_0(f(a)) = refl{t} (source lines 198-211).

Produce I_0 and I_1 from the epimorphism property: the two pairs (iota, refl) and (const_t, alpha_1) both inhabit sm{h:B->C_f} iota o f ~ h o f, so the dual of the author's monomorphism clause (iii) together with function extensionality gives a path gamma between them; I_0 is happly of the first projection of gamma and I_1 follows from the second projection by transport in path types and the fact that transport precomposing with f commutes with happly (source lines 212-225).

From a contractible cone to surjectivity: define a family P : C_f -> prop by recursion on C_f with P(t) := unit and P(iota(b)) := mere-fibre of f at b, check the meridian condition by observing that the fibre at f(a) is inhabited and a mere proposition hence contractible, and conclude that each P(iota(b)) is contractible because C_f is contractible (source lines 227-242).

From surjectivity to epimorphism: for g, h : B -> C with g o f = h o f, chain the four equivalences prd{b:B} g(b) = h(b) to prd{a:A} g(f(a)) = h(f(a)), the middle step using that g(b) = h(b) is a mere proposition because C is a set, and conclude from the assumed element of the last type (source lines 244-256).

proof_roadmap.step: Assume f is an epimorphism and reduce contractibility of C_f to the two induction clauses I_0 and I_1.
Build both clauses from a path between two elements of a sigma type of homotopies, using the dual monomorphism criterion.
Assume C_f contractible, define the prop-valued family P by recursion and conclude surjectivity.
Assume surjectivity and identify g and h by the equivalence chain prd{b} g(b)=h(b) ~ prd{a} g(f(a))=h(f(a)).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.4 at source lines 172-195: for a function f : A -> B between sets, being an epimorphism, having contractible mapping cone C_f, and being surjective are equivalent. The 61-line proof contains no citation: the first direction reduces contractibility of C_f to two induction clauses (lines 198-211) and then manufactures both of them out of a path between two elements of sm{h:B->C_f} iota o f ~ h o f, which is obtained from the dual of the author's monomorphism criterion together with function extensionality and transport in path types (lines 212-225). The second direction defines a prop-valued family on C_f by recursion, which forces a check of the meridian condition via the contractibility of an inhabited mere proposition (lines 227-242), and the third direction is a four-step equivalence chain that uses that the codomain C is a set (lines 244-256). The three directions live in different types and their bookkeeping is not recorded in the statement.
